values.AssociatedLNGNotes: An Oil and Gas Journal article from 2024 says the line would carry Permian gas to the Gulf Coast, including growing demand from LNG export plants. No single terminal is named.

records.researcher_notes: LNG export demand is one of several named drivers. The article names no terminal, so the terminal cell stays blank. The August 2026 trade press says the interstate project was suspended and may become an intrastate line; that does not change the tie.

verifications.note: Record of decision describes the 700-foot, 42-inch pipeline bypass connecting the former UTOS and HIOS systems for the Delfin LNG deepwater port.

values.AssociatedLNGNotes: The EIA pipeline projects list says this line was deferred until after phase 1 of the Driftwood LNG project. A 2019 Houston Chronicle article says Tellurian opened capacity bookings on it days after Driftwood LNG got its federal permit.

records.researcher_notes: Driftwood LNG is now the Woodside Louisiana LNG terminal, so I used that name from the terminal list. The sources say Driftwood. The tie is to Driftwood feedgas supply, stated by EIA and implied by the press timing.
